content.value_statement: Scaling campaigns can lose efficiency when creative fatigue and audience saturation look similar. This skill compares trend data with an early-flight baseline and recommends rotate, widen, or hold.
actual_capabilities: Compares current frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach with an early-flight baseline.
Builds a slope-based trend diagnosis instead of relying on one-day metrics.
Distinguishes creative fatigue from audience saturation using reach and frequency patterns.
Returns one rotate-creative, widen-audience, or hold recommendation per ad set.
Flags questionable conversion tracking before trusting CVR-based conclusions.
Labels figures as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
limitations: Requires a daily or weekly time series and cannot diagnose from a single-day snapshot.
Cannot assess ad sets that remain in the learning phase.
Does not create replacement ads or compute the RQS gate score.
Frequency ceilings depend on campaign objectives and supplied benchmarks.

use_cases.title: Review a scaling campaign
use_cases.description: Identify whether declining performance requires new creative, a wider audience, or no immediate change.

use_cases.title: Triage multiple client ad sets
use_cases.description: Apply consistent baseline and decay checks across exported campaign data.

use_cases.title: Validate conversion decay
use_cases.description: Compare platform CVR with analytics and order data before changing campaign strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Quick fatigue check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ad-set time series. Compare frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach with the early-flight baseline, then recommend rotate, widen, or hold.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one ad set

prompt_templates.title: Baseline and decay review
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the first stable post-learning window. Measure frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach changes from that baseline and explain the dominant cause.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-set campaign triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze each ad set separately. Return one trigger per set, name the threshold used, and mark incomplete rows as unavailable.

prompt_templates.title: Measurement-aware diagnosis
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare platform, GA4, and ecommerce exports. Verify conversion tracking, separate fatigue from saturation, and route unreliable signals to the account auditor.

output_examples.input: Frequency rose from 2.1 to 6.2, CTR fell 48 percent, CVR stayed stable, and reach continued growing.
output: Diagnosis: Creative fatigue is the dominant cause.
Reason: CTR decayed while frequency increased, but audience reach continued expanding.

output_examples.input: Retargeting reach plateaued, frequency climbed, and both CTR and CVR declined across two weeks.
output: Diagnosis: Audience saturation is the dominant cause.
Caveat: Confirm the CVR decline against analytics or order data.

output_examples.input: The user provides only current-day frequency and CTR values for an ad set still in learning.
output_examples.output: No fatigue decision is available. Request a time series and the learning-exit date before evaluating decay.

best_practices: Use the first stable window after learning as the fixed baseline.
Confirm reach and frequency behavior before naming fatigue or saturation.
Check CVR against analytics or order data when conversion tracking may be unreliable.
anti_patterns: Do not diagnose fatigue from a single-day snapshot.
Do not apply one universal frequency threshold to every objective.
Do not present inferred causes or estimates as measured facts.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide daily or weekly impressions, reach, frequency, CTR, CVR, spend, and the learning-exit date when available.

faq.question: Can it work with one day of data?
faq.answer: No. A reliable fatigue diagnosis requires a trend against an early-flight baseline.

faq.question: How does it separate fatigue from saturation?
faq.answer: Creative fatigue combines rising frequency and falling CTR with growing reach. Saturation combines rising frequency with plateauing reach and broader decay.

faq.question: Does it use a universal frequency limit?
faq.answer: No. The working ceiling depends on the objective, audience type, and supplied measurement guidance.

faq.question: What happens when conversion tracking is unreliable?
faq.answer: The skill flags the measurement risk and avoids a CVR-based action until the signal is verified.

faq.question: Does it create replacement ad creative?
faq.answer: No. It diagnoses the issue and routes rotate recommendations to a separate creative-building skill.
